title: Allow explicit runs to drain a paused Dag
body: A paused Dag cannot execute an explicitly triggered run without changing its scheduling state. Unpausing also resumes the schedule, which is undesirable for Dags used to reprocess historical data on demand. This change lets manual runs, backfills, and asset materializations put the Dag into the existing `draining` state. Unfinished runs can start or resume, the scheduler creates no scheduled or asset-triggered runs, and the Dag returns to paused when its unfinished runs finish. Runs held by a paused backfill remain held; that backfill must be resumed for its runs to finish and draining to complete. The state change affects the whole Dag. A paused Dag still starts nothing: draining clears its paused state, without adding a per-run override or changing the scheduler's paused checks. closes: #60768 - The trigger, backfill, and materialization forms offer **Unpause** (the default), **Drain**, and **Keep paused**. Unpause resumes the schedule; Drain allows unfinished runs to finish without resuming the schedule; Keep paused leaves the Dag paused. Paused backfills remain paused under every choice. - Unpause and Drain show the count of unfinished runs that can proceed. The count waits for fresh backfill state and excludes runs held by a paused backfill. The options have an accessible radio-group label. - Forms wait for the Dag-state refresh before allowing submission. A denied drain reports the missing edit permission; choosing Keep paused clears the error and allows retrying without reopening the form. - `POST /dags/{dag_id}/dagRuns`, `POST /backfills`, and `POST /assets/{asset_id}/materialize` accept `drain_dag`, defaulting to `false`. Draining requires Dag edit permission in addition to the existing creation permission. On an active Dag, it stops scheduling and leaves the Dag paused after its unfinished runs finish. - `airflowctl dags trigger` and `airflowctl backfill create` expose `--drain-dag`. Default fields are omitted from outgoing requests for compatibility with older strict API models, while required nullable `logical_date` is preserved. The drain state change commits or rolls back with run creation. Backfill creation retains its early backfill-row commit, then creates the runs before taking the Dag drain lock, keeping that lock out of the bulk insertion work. The scheduler's initializing-backfill guard covers this interval. The pre-existing finalizer race for a Dag that is already draining remains outside this change, as described in the [review discussion](https://github.com/apache/airflow/pull/73763#discussion_r4158824465). Documentation, the existing drain release note, API descriptions, and generated clients describe the paused-backfill exception. Validation: 56 affected UI tests and 27 airflowctl operation tests passed. PostgreSQL API/model/scheduler tests and rollback/cleanup tests passed; the independent-session lock tests passed on both PostgreSQL and MySQL. Regular and manual prek checks, including the production UI build, passed. The radio-card layout: | Trigger form | Drain selected | Backfill form | | --- | --- | --- | | | | | These existing screenshots show the layout; the updated descriptions also explain that paused backfills stay paused. --- ##### Was generative AI tooling used to co-author this PR? - [X] Yes — Claude Code (Opus 5.5), Codex (GPT-6) Generated-by: Claude Code (Opus 5.5), Codex (GPT-6) following [the guidelines](https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/main/contributing-docs/05_pull_requests.rst#gen-ai-assisted-contributions)

+A manual run, backfill or asset materialization on a paused Dag can drain the Dag instead of unpausing it.
+Choose **Drain** under **Dag is paused** in the UI form, or set ``drain_dag`` to ``true`` in the REST API
+request. This changes the whole Dag, not only the new run: unfinished Dag runs can start or resume, except
+those held by paused backfills. Paused backfills remain paused, and their unfinished runs prevent draining
+from completing until those backfills are resumed and their runs finish. The scheduler creates no scheduled
+or asset-triggered Dag runs, and the Dag pauses again once all unfinished runs finish. The Dag starts draining
+in the same transaction that creates the run, so if the run is rejected, the Dag stays paused. Setting ``drain_dag`` on an
+active Dag drains it the same way, so the Dag also ends up paused. Because it changes the Dag's scheduling
+state, ``drain_dag`` requires the same permission as pausing the Dag, in addition to the permission to create
+the run.
+
 Dags can be deactivated (do not confuse it with ``Active`` tag in the UI) by removing them from the

 before and stored in the database it will set is as deactivated. The metadata and history of the

+    @classmethod
+    def start_drain(cls, dag_id: str, *, session: Session) -> None:
+        """
+        Put the Dag into the draining state.
+
+        Lock the Dag row and change its scheduling state in the caller's transaction.
+        Call this in the transaction that creates the explicit runs so the state change
+        commits or rolls back with them.
+        """
+        dag_model = session.scalars(
+            with_row_locks(
+                select(cls).where(cls.dag_id == dag_id), of=cls, session=session
+            ).execution_options(populate_existing=True)
+        ).one()
+        dag_model.set_scheduling_state(DagSchedulingState.DRAINING)
